skill.name: authoring-a-policy-standard
skill.description: Author or expand one rules-first policy standard with explicit given, found, proposed, and not-defined provenance. Use for a single governed policy subject; do not use for schema drift, Process definitions, or provider write mechanics.
skill.shortDescription: Build one provenance-complete rules-first policy standard.
skill.defaultPrompt: Use $authoring-a-policy-standard to prepare this subject's policy without inventing rules or hiding unresolved decisions.

instructions: Name one policy subject and inspect the configured policy registry for an exact existing definition before choosing create or expansion.
Treat a batch as separate subject-level decisions even when their review is presented together.
Bind the applicable portable policy shape, source authorities, and current target identity before drafting.
flexibility: Several subjects may share one review meeting, but each keeps a separate draft, decision list, proposal list, and confirmation scope.
stopConditions: Stop when subject identity, existing-record identity, or governing policy shape is ambiguous.

instructions: Collect definition, classifications, rules, lifecycle, and change expectations from the operator and named sources.
Mark each fact as given, found, or proposed; record exact source identity for every found fact.
Treat schema names, types, options, and relations as found structure only; any claim about meaning, requirement, or determination logic remains proposed unless another authority states it.
flexibility: Draft as few or as many proposals as useful, but keep every proposal explicit and separately reviewable.
stopConditions: Stop before presenting inferred schema semantics as organization policy.

instructions: Apply the governed policy-standard section order and coverage derivations to the exact subject.
Write bare not defined for a required policy decision that has no authoritative value; do not omit it or turn it into a guess.
Keep not defined distinct from a proposed value awaiting explicit acceptance.
stopConditions: Stop if the registered shape or a required section cannot be resolved from the selected Context contract.

instructions: Resolve every named relation target against the current configured registry or provider authority.
For open-ended linked-process discovery, perform one bounded registry query and one bounded keyword pass.
Record positive matches as proposals and record the exact lookup attempt when no match exists.
flexibility: A bounded lookup is sufficient; do not expand into an unbounded workspace crawl.
stopConditions: Stop before writing not defined for a relation that the configured authority can answer.

instructions: Present the complete draft together with a decisions-needed list and a proposals-awaiting-confirmation list.
Require an explicit decision for each subject and each proposed rule; urgency or polished prose never substitutes for confirmation.
Keep declined proposals out of the current-state document.
flexibility: Compress the visual presentation when useful, but preserve itemized decisions and exact subject scopes.
stopConditions: Stop before any write while proposals, not-defined decisions, or subject-level confirmations remain unresolved.

instructions: After separate exact authority exists, create or update the single current policy record through the configured capability and include one versioned change-log entry.
Remove proposed markers only from accepted values and apply any required schema or option change in the same governed batch rather than claiming an unimplemented rule.
Re-fetch the written record and verify the complete shape, accepted values, change-log entry, and absence of unresolved proposal residue.
stopConditions: Stop before provider effects when the compiler, exact approval, single-use start, or read-after-write verification is unavailable.

verification: Exactly one current policy record exists for the selected subject.
Every durable rule is given or found, or was explicitly accepted from the proposal list.
Every unresolved decision is visibly not defined and never silently absent.
Every relation is resolved or carries the bounded lookup evidence that established a real gap.
Any applied write is re-read with its change log and no proposed-marker residue.

gotchas.summary: A complete-looking policy can hide that every substantive rule was invented from a skeleton or schema under deadline pressure.
gotchas.countermeasure: Expose all proposals in a separate decision list and require itemized subject-level confirmation.

gotchas.summary: A schema proves that fields and values exist but does not prove what the organization means by them or when they are required.
gotchas.countermeasure: Mark inferred meaning as proposed unless an exact policy authority supplies it.

gotchas.summary: A resolvable relation can be mislabeled not defined when the author skips the configured registry lookup.
gotchas.countermeasure: Perform the bounded lookup first and reserve not defined for unanswered policy decisions.

gotchas.summary: Leaving declined proposals or accepted proposal markers in the durable document makes current policy ambiguous.
gotchas.countermeasure: Drop declined proposals and remove markers only from explicitly accepted values before verification.

limitations: This procedural guide does not create policy, provider-write, approval, or execution authority.
Adoption requires independent exact host-skill behavior evidence and a separate governed fallback-removal decision.
